notes:
Background: mid-market product/SaaS company building an in-app AI assistant and enhanced search. Product and infra teams are evaluating Redwood as primary inference platform. Primary constraint: EU data residency (data at rest + inference logs).

Conversation summary: started with Hosted API to move fast; Hosted used for early integration tests. After seeing cost/throughput profiles, team is evaluating a Dedicated pool in EU to get predictable latency and better unit economics for heavy in-product usage. They want the same API surface for both Hosted -> Dedicated to avoid code changes.

Key technical requirements / asks:
- Residency: "EU-only" for customer data and inference logs; no US access unless explicit legal exception. Quote from product lead: "EU-only data is non-negotiable for our enterprise contracts."
- Latency targets: 99th percentile <120ms for short chat requests (up to 256 tokens); p50 target ~40-60ms.  Throughput target ~200 concurrent qps during peak, burst to 500 qps acceptable for short periods.
- Cost sensitivity: mid-market budget; looking for Dedicated commit that brings 30-50% cost reduction vs hosted at current volumes.
- Model preferences: prefer Redwood-verified quantized models (Llama3-derived / open variants) with automatic fallback to smaller/cheaper model under load. Need confirmation of which model variants are hosted in eu-west region.
- Routing/fallback: want primary routing to EU Dedicated, with multi-region read-only fallback in case of regional outage. Legal team concerned about cross-border fallbacks; they asked for a plan that keeps PII in EU and only uses non-PII for cross-region fallback.
- Security: SSO/SAML, KMS integration for customer keys, retention controls on logs (30/90/365 day options), audit logging and certs (SOC2, ISO).
- Observability: token-level cost breakdown, per-route latency heatmaps, 99p tracing for tail latency analysis.

POC plan / milestones:
- Week 1: EU-hosted POC with synthetic traffic (2k users/day equivalent) to gather p50/p90/p99 latency and cost per 1k tokens. Collect streaming behavior and function-calls.
- Week 2: Security/infra runbook review with CISO and infra. Test KMS workflows (bring-your-own-key) and SSO flow.
- Post-POC: SE to produce Dedicated sizing and cost model, include autoscale / burst config options and expected per-token pricing.

Open questions / tradeoffs discussed:
- Multi-region routing vs strict EU-only residency: tradeoff between availability and compliance. Options discussed: active-active EU regions with warm replicas, active EU + cold non-EU fallback (only for non-sensitive requests), or full EU-only Dedicated with cross-region fallback disabled.
- Latency vs cost: smaller quantized models reduce cost but risk quality regressions; team wants A/B on relevance and hallucination rates before committing.
- KV/prefix caching: Redwood Optimize suggestions could reduce token usage significantly; SE recommended synthetic run showing 20-30% token savings for our common chat patterns.

Stakeholders:
- Product Lead: Emilie Novak (owner of use-case), emphasized EU residency and latency SLAs.
- Head of Infra: Tomasz Kaczmarek — wants VPC peering and BYOK KMS flow.
- Legal: reviewing SCCs and DPA clauses for cross-border fallback.

Next steps (agreed):
1) Start EU-hosted POC next week (Jordan to schedule) — FF meeting/tracking in Fireflies ff-20260224-3434.
2) SE Marina to deliver sizing + dedicated price sheet within 5 business days after POC.
3) Legal and Security to finalize acceptable fallback patterns (EU-only vs EU-primary with redaction).
4) Prepare draft SOW for Dedicated if POC meets 99p latency SLOs and cost targets.
